text:
marco: quick thought — propose we split the regional VPC edge proxy into lightweight per-tenant shards (shard-per-subnet) to give strong egress-ip affinity and reduce noisy-tenant tail latencies. want tradeoffs on DNS, control-plane coupling, and rollout.
anya: can you summarize the main goals? is this primarily about preserving source IP for customer whitelists or isolation for noisy workloads?
liz: both. biggest ops issue today is noisy tenants causing proxy queue buildup and changing observed egress IPs during scale events. per-tenant shards would keep egress ip stable and localize overload.
marco: exactly — two wins: 1) predictable egress IPs for customers who need fixed ips, 2) less blast radius when a tenant spikes. downside is more endpoints to manage and potential route53 churn.
sam: curious about cost/scale: more shards = more connections and idle capacity. do we have metrics on percent of requests per tenant that would justify dedicated shards?
rachel: we can start with a hybrid: shard top 1% by QPS, keep the rest on shared regional pool. that reduces explosion while protecting heavy tenants.
anya: how would control plane separation look? do we need a separate CP per shard or just tenant-aware routing in the existing CP?
marco: want minimal CP surface: keep single control plane but add a "shard affinity" mapping service that assigns tenants -> shard endpoints. mapping stored in CP DB; dataplane uses that mapping to route. no per-shard CP instances.
liz: mapping service sounds ok but we need failover semantics: if mapping store is unreachable, dataplane should fallback to regional shared proxy (with a telemetry event). we must avoid blackholing.
sre-bot: deploy-bot scheduled: canary-create shard-mapper v0.1 on staging at 2025-06-03T15:00:00Z :rocket:
marco: rollout plan suggestion: 1) implement shard-mapper + routing logic behind feature flag; 2) create tooling to provision shards and attach nat/elastic-ip; 3) canary with top-10 tenants on staging; 4) do prod canary with single region and two tenants; 5) gradual scale to top 1% then evaluate.
sam: operational playbook items: auto-scale thresholds, alert when shard CPU > 60% for 5m, cost tag per-shard, automated deprovision when inactive for 24h. also add per-shard e2e healthchecks and synthetic probes.
rachel: DNS cutover approach: use short TTL CNAMEs for shard endpoints and a global route53 alias for fallback. change flow: create shard endpoint -> provision EIP -> add CNAME pointing tenant.example -> monitor for 30m -> flip traffic. rollback by removing CNAME and relying on global alias.
marco: question for security folks: do we want TLS terminated at shard or keep TLS passthrough and terminate at shared TLS gateway? TLS termination at shard simplifies policy but spreads certs.
liz: my preference is passthrough + mutual-tls at shared ingress, then shard terminates TLS only for customers who opted-in. avoids cert ops explosion.
anya: can we do SNI routing at L4 to send to shards without terminating? that would preserve crypto but allows routing by hostname.
marco: yeah SNI-based routing is viable for host-based customers. need to evaluate for connection-intensive workloads where SNI handshake cost matters.
sam: small ask: add telemetry tags: shard_id, tenant_id, egress_ip, pool_type. that'll make billing & debugging easier.
rachel: ops checklist for cutover: cert readiness, EIP quota checks, route53 automations, shard tagging, incident playbook. i'll draft a runbook.
marco: thanks all — next step i'll post a short RFC with mapping service API and provisioning CLI. if nobody objects, i'll kick off the staging canary on the deploy-bot window. :thumbsup:
